beats.headline: Three billion star systems
beats.text: Over three billion independent star systems. Its rules are the ones Earth was seized under, and every season a new Dungeon Crawler World debuts across its net for quintillions of citizens to become obsessed with. It is the law and the audience at once.

beats.headline: Seeded, then harvested
beats.text: There are six starter species the Syndicate uses to seed worlds, and humans are one of them. Find a compatible planet, sprinkle them on, wait a couple of thousand years, then reveal yourself to the largest settlement once there is a working government. That counts as first contact in the legal sense. Earth then had fifty years to claim itself as a sovereign entity, and first contact was several thousand years ago, around the time the pyramids went up. Earth defaulted. Borant has a backlog of worlds to mine, and this one's time has come.

beats.headline: Culture, planted in advance
beats.text: Carl wonders why alien pigs wear tuxedos. Brandon has already asked Mistress Tiatha about the fire-breathing monkeys in lederhosen, and passes on her answer, stopping halfway through the name with a glance at the ceiling: the Syndicate not only seeded Earth with people millions of years ago but kept people here the whole time, some of them humans from other worlds, steering culture, inventing things, writing books and songs that already existed elsewhere. Why, Brandon cannot say. They only see what they are shown.

beats.headline: The Indigenous Species Protection Act
beats.text: Both Earth boxes come with an Earth Hobby Potion, which, per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, the Syndicate Government requires be awarded to all crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. It is optional, cannot be sold or transferred, and grants a random level-three Earth hobby. The AI's own description complains about the lawyers making it put their crap in. Carl wonders whether it is a bureaucratic attempt at preserving Earth culture, and is reminded of the military.

beats.headline: One veto a season
beats.text: The AI rules that Carl's detonator came through both precursor bursts; Borant appeals, and a Syndicate court overrules it, adding that the achievements from the explosion are just and must be paid. But Syndicate rules give every host a single veto each season, almost always saved for the tenth floor or deeper. Borant spends it on the third. The Syndicate also taxes every non-sponsored box, allowing only a handful of free Celestials a season, and an emergency session is now deciding whether Borant pays for the other eighty-two.

beats.headline: Seven factions lose in court
beats.text: Seven factions sue to take the Gate of the Feral Gods from Carl, naming him and the AI as co-defendants, and the Syndicate Court finds for the defence. He collects seven Fight the Power achievements, stock certificates, and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: The Walk-On list
beats.text: Survivors on the surface are natives, and by the rules untouchable; their implants are scrambled once the crawl starts. So when producers want a particular native, a Walk-On list goes out, and bounty crews sneak onto a planet closed to non-natives to take them. It is not remotely legal. The Syndicate knows, rights groups complain, and nothing happens, though its security still patrols and still catches trespassers. This season's list includes a woman in the tropics, a little girl's father, a goat, a dead crawler's twin and a cat.

beats.headline: A headquarters in Florida
beats.text: The Syndicate's presence in the system now runs out of a temporary headquarters on the Eastern Seaboard of North America, with Prime Minister Victory and her staff. They chose an area they believed had minimal surviving native life, somewhere in the state of Florida, and the moment they set down the natives were all over them. Orbit belongs to the Open Intellect Action Network, and Borant has nobody spare to watch the feeds. For now, it is busy.

beats.headline: A suicide mission, from security
beats.text: Captain Fresh of Syndicate security says it plainly to the soldier going in under a dead fan's name: it is a suicide mission. The Syndicate is trying to nuke the whole system off the map before it spreads further, and losing; the AI stops everything and answers in kind. A surgical crawler kill, they believe, will destabilise the group, start the Ascendency game early and let their other assets move. It is us or them, he says. The viewers who will not stop watching are to blame too.
